# Adjudication Task — Chapter 635

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃635화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|띠링.
  6|
  7|
  8|
  9|- [애뇌산의 망령(亡靈)]이 나타났습니다!
 10|
 11|
 12|
 13|애뇌산의 망령.
 14|
 15|본 적도, 들은 적도 없는 존재와 이름.
 16|
 17|그러나 새롭게 전달받은 정보를 미처 이해하기도 전에, 시스템으로부터 애뇌산의 망령이라 칭해지는 거대한 흑호(黑虎)가 천둥 같은 포효를 내질렀다.
 18|
 19|- 크와아아앙!
 20|
 21|어둠을 찢으며 산 전체를 울리는 포효에, 주위의 공기가 물결처럼 일렁이고 풀이며 나뭇가지가 산산이 부서진다.
 22|
 23|그것은 단순한 맹수의 울부짖음이 아니었다.
 24|
 25|마음속 깊숙한 곳에 숨어 있던 두려움을 불러일으키고, 나아가 심령(心靈)마저 뒤흔드는 원초적인 무언가였다.
 26|
 27|그리고 나는 이 힘의 정체를, 이 세상에서 누구보다 잘 알고 있는 사람이었고.
 28|
 29|‘피어(Fear).’
 30|
 31|처음 놈의 청백색 눈동자를 마주한 순간부터 본능적으로 깨달았다.
 32|
 33|갑작스럽게 나타난 저 거대한 맹수는 짐승이라는 두 글자로 완전히 담을 수 없는 존재라는 것을.
 34|
 35|그리고 이러한 느낌이 마냥 낯설게 느껴지지 않는 이유는, 이미 몇 달 전 호북에서 놈과 닮은 어떤 존재를 맞닥트린 경험 덕분이었다.
 36|
 37|‘수신룡(水神龍).’
 38|
 39|암천에 의하여 이지를 상실한 채 미쳐 날뛰던 동정호의 주인. 수백 년의 세월 끝에 새로운 영역으로 접어든 희대의 영물.
 40|
 41|나는 태산처럼 우뚝 선 흑호에게서 수신룡과 같은 기운을 읽었고, 그것은 비단 나 혼자만 느낀 것이 아니었다.
 42|
 43|- 끄으으응…….
 44|
 45|평범한 기준에는 영물이라 칭하기에 부족함이 없는 백호였지만, 강렬한 피어를 이기기에는 역부족이었다.
 46|
 47|하지만 겁먹은 강아지처럼 끙끙거리는 녀석과는 달리, 또 다른 누군가는 한 치의 망설임도 없이 앞으로 나섰다.
 48|
 49|“네놈의 소행이더냐!”
 50|
 51|콰앙!
 52|
 53|분노가 가득 담긴 외침과 함께, 힘껏 지면을 박찬 야수묘왕의 신형이 눈 깜짝할 사이에 십여 장의 거리를 지우며 쏘아진다.
 54|
 55|어느새 힘껏 말아쥔 주먹에서 눈부신 광휘(光輝)가 터져 나왔다.
 56|
 57|후우웅!
 58|
 59|묵직한 파공성. 주먹을 실타래처럼 휘감은 파괴적인 강기가 막아서는 모든 것을 지우며 나아갔다.
 60|
 61|그리고 그 끝에…….
 62|
 63|솨아아악!
 64|
 65|아무것도 없는, 텅 빈 허공이 있었다.
 66|
 67|“……!”
 68|
 69|“……!”
 70|
 71|피했다. 다른 누구도 아닌 십왕(十王)에 속한 초절정 고수의 일권을.
 72|
 73|그야말로 찰나지간에 벌어진 일이었고, 어둠 속에서 안개처럼 움직여 야수묘왕의 공격을 피한 흑호는 밤처럼 까맣고 커다란 자신의 앞발을 휘둘렀다.
 74|
 75|쉬익!
 76|
 77|믿을 수 없을 만큼 빠르고. 강맹하게.
 78|
 79|꽈앙! 콰드드득!
 80|
 81|굉음과 함께 막대한 충격파가 사방을 휩쓸었다. 순간적으로 가해진 거력을 버티지 못하고 밀려난 야수묘왕이 눈을 부릅떴다.
 82|
 83|“이게 무슨……!”
 84|
 85|그러나 그에게는 경악할 만한 시간조차 충분히 주어지지 않았다. 먹잇감을 앞에 둔 배고픈 맹수는 망설이지 않는 법이니까.
 86|
 87|- 크아아앙!
 88|
 89|다시 한번 터져 나온 외침이 애뇌산을 뒤흔들었다.
 90|
 91|게이트와 몬스터가 상식이자 일상이 되어 버린 현대라면 모를까. 이 세상의 무림인들은 피어에 익숙하지 않다.
 92|
 93|더군다나 예상을 아득히 뛰어넘는 규격 외의 존재를 처음으로 조우하게 되어 당황한 야수묘왕의 경우에는 더더욱 그럴 수밖에 없었다.
 94|
 95|“흡!”
 96|
 97|아주 미세한 경직. 야수묘왕으로서는 최선의 결과였겠지만, 높은 경지에 이른 이들의 생사결은 바로 그 한순간에 노출된 틈새로 결정되는 법.
 98|
 99|상대가 무인이 아닌 맹수라 해도 그 사실은 달라지지 않는다.
100|
101|쉬이이익!
102|
103|느려진 세상 속, 흡사 갈고리와도 같은 흑호의 발톱이 바람을 찢은 그때.
104|
105|내 손아귀를 떠난 한 자루의 창이 눈부신 빛줄기가 되어 공간을 가로질렀다.
106|
107|쐐애애액! 콰앙!
108|
109|하늘이 쪼개지는 굉음과 함께 반경 십여 장의 공간이 뒤흔들린다.
110|
111|기운과 기운. 힘과 힘의 격돌.
112|
113|그리고 짧은 순간 벌어진 격돌의 승자는 바로 나였다.
114|
115|콰드드득!
116|
117|창과 한 몸이 되어 뒤로 튕겨 나간 거대한 흑호의 몸뚱어리가 어둠이 내려앉은 숲 너머로 사라지자, 저 멀리 한곳에 모여 있던 수십 그루의 거목이 꺾이고 흔들렸다.
118|
119|진즉 잠에서 깨어 숨죽인 채 이곳을 바라보고 있었을 산 새가 일제히 날아오르고, 수많은 잎사귀와 나뭇가지가 소나기처럼 쏟아졌다.
120|
121|투둑. 파사삭!
122|
123|놈을 잡으려면 바로 지금이 적기다.
124|
125|그러나 곧장 흑호를 쫓아가려던 나는 이내 얼마 되지 않아 걸음을 멈출 수밖에 없었다.
126|
127|‘어째서 기척이…….’
128|
129|기척이 느껴지지 않는다. 조금도.
130|
131|그나마 있는 단서라고는 폭탄이라도 터진 것처럼 난장판이 된 잔해와 창날이 부서진 채로 떨어져 있는 창 한 자루가 전부.
132|
133|그 외에는 어떤 족적이나 혈흔도 찾아볼 수 없었다.
134|
135|‘내 기감의 범위를 벗어났다고? 그것도 이 정도로 빠르게?’
136|
137|주위를 노려보고 있던 그때. 백호와 함께 달려온 야수묘왕이 분노와 부끄러움이 뒤섞인 표정으로 입을 열었다.
138|
139|“놈은?”
140|
141|“도망친 것 같습니다. 찾을 수가 없어요.”
142|
143|“……빌어먹을. 못 볼 꼴을 보였군.”
144|
145|“이해합니다. 빈말이 아니라 진심으로요.”
146|
147|문경과 적천강도 수신룡이 발산하는 피어에 잠시나마 동요했던 적이 있었다.
148|
149|야수묘왕은 십왕에 꼽힌 만큼 대단한 고수지만, 인외(人外)의 경지에 다다른 두 사람과 비교하는 것은 무리다.
150|
151|오히려 역으로 생각하면 야수묘왕은 짐작했던 것 이상으로 빠르게 피어의 영향에서 벗어난 셈이었다.
152|
153|그것이 남만이라는 지역의 특성상 어릴 적부터 기이한 독물이나 맹수들을 자주 접해서인지는 모르겠지만.
154|
155|그나저나 지금 당장 중요한 건…….
156|
157|“놈이 아직 살아 있습니다. 혈흔이 없는 걸 보니 딱히 상처를 입은 것 같지도 않고요.”
158|
159|낮게 깔린 내 목소리에 야수묘왕이 고개를 끄덕였다.
160|
161|“그럴 것 같았다. 피하지 못할 것을 알자 마지막 순간에 창날을 물더군. 그것도 분명히 강기가 서려 있던 창날을. 남만에서 일평생을 살았지만 저런 놈은 지금까지 본 적도, 들은 적도 없다.”
162|
163|“그건 아닐걸요.”
164|
165|“아니라니. 뭘 말이냐?”
166|
167|“마지막에 하셨던 말씀이요.”
168|
169|야수묘왕이 뭐라 대답하기도 전에, 나는 담담하게 말을 이었다.
170|
171|“본 적이 없더라도, 들은 적은 있으실 겁니다. 분명히.”
172|
173|당장은 기척이 느껴지지 않지만, 언제 다시 놈이 튀어나올지 모르는 상황.
174|
175|자연스럽게 나와 등을 맞댄 채 주위를 경계하던 야수묘왕의 몸이 흠칫 굳었다.
176|
177|“혹시.”
178|
179|“아마도 지금 생각하고 계신 게 맞을 겁니다. 호북성에서 비슷한 일이 있었거든요.”
180|
181|“……그 이무기를 말하는 것이냐?”
182|
183|신음처럼 중얼거린 야수묘왕이 말을 이었다.
184|
185|“무림맹으로부터 받은 서신에 그런 내용이 있긴 했지. 하지만 내심 허황된 이야기라 여겼다.”
186|
187|“아니, 남만야수궁주 맞습니까? 당장 하나뿐인 아들놈이 백호를 타고 돌아다니는 마당에 그걸 왜 못 믿어요?”
188|
189|“백호를 타지, 이무기를 타고 있지는 않으니까.”
190|
191|“……아.”
192|
193|그것도 그러네.
194|
195|하긴 이무기는 신화 속에서나 등장하는 존재다. 정보의 출처가 무림맹이라고 해도 쉽게 믿어지지 않는 건 당연하지.
196|
197|짧고 굵은 대답에 할 말이 없어진 나를 향해, 야수묘왕이 불쑥 입을 열었다.
198|
199|“그렇다면 방금 나타났던 놈도 남천마후, 그 요녀(妖女)의 손이 닿은 것이냐?”
200|
201|“확신은 못 합니다. 하지만 그럴 가능성이 높겠죠.”
202|
203|아니라고 단언하기에는 석연치 않은 점이 한둘이 아니다.
204|
205|옛 오독문의 본거지였다고는 하나 장장 백여 년 동안이나 잠잠했던 애뇌산에서 갑작스럽게 이런 참사가 벌어진 것도, 갑작스럽게 등장한 흑호의 강력함도 과거의 수신룡과 겹쳐 보이는 듯했다.
206|
207|‘애뇌산의 망령이라니.’
208|
209|도대체 놈의 진정한 정체가 뭘까.
210|
211|이 자리에 싸늘한 주검이 되어 널브러진 이들 외에도 남아 있어야 할 이백 명의 전사와 그들이 부리는 맹수들은 어디에 있는 것일까.
212|
213|내가 무거운 눈빛으로 주위를 훑어보던 그 순간.
214|
215|- 크르륵.
216|
217|피어의 영향에서 간신히 빠져나왔던 백호가 갑자기 자세를 낮추고 꼬리를 바짝 치켜세웠다.
218|
219|그 사실이 의미하는 바를 깨달은 나와 야수묘왕이 반사적으로 고개를 돌렸을 때, 저 멀리에서는 어둠이 일렁이고 있었다.
220|
221|‘저건……!’
222|
223|나도, 야수묘왕도 다른 이야기를 나누느라 잠시 간과하고 있었다.
224|
225|동물의 후각은 인간보다 수십. 수백 배는 뛰어나며, 주로 밤에 사냥을 나서는 호랑이는 그만큼 후각이 뛰어나다는 것을.
226|
227|그 말은 즉.
228|
229|‘이 녀석의 후각이, 내가 느낄 수 있는 기감의 범위보다 넓다.’
230|
231|한 줄기 깨달음과 동시에, 나와 야수묘왕은 동시에 지면을 박찼다.
232|
233|
234|
235|* * *
236|
237|
238|
239|놈을 쫓는 과정에서 똑똑히 알게 됐다.
240|
241|왜 사람들이 호랑이를 산군(山君)이라 부르는지.
242|
243|‘아. 저 씨벌놈 보게.’
244|
245|나는 내심 욕을 삼키며 저 멀리 달려나가는 검은 동체(動體)를 노려보았다.
246|
247|굽이굽이 진 산줄기를 아무리 달려도, 구름과 안개에 덮인 봉우리를 타고 넘어도 놈을 따라잡을 수가 없다.
248|
249|놈은 강력한 힘과 지치지 않는 체력. 그리고 신출귀몰한 움직임으로 시종일관 나와 야수묘왕을 앞질렀고, 어디 가서 흰 털 좀 뱉는다는 영물인 백호조차 놈을 따라잡을 수 없었다.
250|
251|아니, 오히려 점점 불안해하고 있었다.
252|
253|‘그럴 만도 하지. 상대는 평범한 호랑이가 아니니까.’
254|
255|산군은 산의 왕이라는 뜻 외에도 산신령을 칭하는 단어이기도 한데, 저놈은 애뇌산의 신령이 아니라 망령이다. 아니, 어쩌면 그보다 더 불길한 악령(惡靈)에 가까울 수도 있다.
256|
257|그리고 쉴 새 없이 흑호를 쫓아 이동하는 도중에 목격한 광경으로 인하여, 그런 생각은 더더욱 굳혀졌다.
258|
259|“이런 찢어 죽일……!”
260|
261|용암처럼 끓어오르는 듯한 음성. 야수묘왕의 분노어린 시선이 향한 곳에는 사지를 축 늘어트린 채 절명한 시신들이 있었다.
262|
263|깊은 골짜기와 절벽 끄트머리. 한때는 맑았을 테지만 이제는 독으로 인해 검게 물든 계곡…….
264|
265|남만 전사들의 시신은 우리가 향하는 길을 따라 이정표처럼 쓰러져 있었고, 바람에 섞여든 혈향과 악취는 지독했다.
266|
267|“감히, 감히 이런 짓을 벌이다니!”
268|
269|주위를 스쳐 지나가는 참혹한 광경을 확인한 야수묘왕의 전신에서 광포한 기파가 흘러넘쳤다.
270|
271|지금 이 순간 그는 어느 때보다 분노하고 있었고, 그만큼 움직임은 거칠어졌다.
272|
273|“노옴!”
274|

“I thought as much. When it knew it couldn’t dodge, it bit down on the spearhead at the last moment. A spearhead wreathed in Force, no less. I’ve lived in Nanman all my life, but I’ve never seen or heard of anything like it.”

[P79]
“I don’t think that’s true.”

[P80]
“What do you mean?”

[P81]
“The last part.”

[P82]
Before he could reply, I went on.

[P83]
“You may never have seen one, but you’ve heard of one. I’m sure of it.”

[P84]
We could not sense the Black Tiger for now, but it might spring out at any moment. The Beast Miao King had put his back to mine as we watched our surroundings. At my words, he stiffened.

[P85]
“Could it be…?”

[P86]
“You’re probably thinking of the right thing. Something similar happened in Hubei Province.”

[P87]
“…You mean that imugi?”

[P88]
The words came out like a groan. He continued, “The Murim Alliance mentioned it in a letter. But I thought the story sounded far-fetched.”

[P89]
“Are you really the Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace? Your only son rides around on a White Tiger, and you couldn’t believe that?”

[P90]
“He rides a White Tiger, not an imugi.”

[P91]
“…Ah.”

[P92]
Fair enough.

[P93]
An imugi belonged in myth. Even coming from the Murim Alliance, the story would have been hard to believe.

[P94]
That short answer left me with nothing to say. Then the Beast Miao King asked, “So was the creature we just saw touched by the Southern Heaven Demon Empress too? That witch?”

[P95]
“I can’t be sure. But it’s likely.”

[P96]
Too much about this felt wrong for me to rule it out.

[P97]
Ailao Mountain had been quiet for more than a hundred years, despite once being the Five Poisons Sect’s headquarters. Now a massacre had happened here, and a Black Tiger of astonishing power had appeared. It all reminded me of the Water God Dragon.

[P98]
*Ailao Mountain’s Wraith.*

[P99]
What was it really?

[P100]
And where were the other two hundred warriors who should still have been here? Where were the beasts they commanded?

[P101]
As I scanned the area, my eyes fell on White Tiger.

[P102]
*Grrr.*

[P103]
Having barely recovered from the Fear, it suddenly crouched low and raised its tail high.

[P104]
The Beast Miao King and I understood what that meant and turned at once.

[P105]
Far away, the darkness was rippling.

[P106]
*That’s…!*

[P107]
We had both overlooked something while we talked.

[P108]
An animal’s sense of smell was dozens, even hundreds of times keener than a human’s. A tiger, which usually hunted at night, had a nose to match.

[P109]
Which meant…

[P110]
*White Tiger can smell farther than my Qi Sense can reach.*

[P111]
The moment it clicked, the Beast Miao King and I kicked off the ground together.

[P112]
* * *

[P113]
As we chased it, I learned exactly why people called tigers mountain lords.[^1]

[P114]
*Ah. Look at that fucking bastard.*

[P115]
I swallowed the curse and glared at the black shape racing far ahead.

[P116]
No matter how far we ran along the winding ridges, no matter how many cloud- and mist-covered peaks we crossed, we could not catch it.

[P117]
Its strength, inexhaustible Stamina, and elusive movements kept it ahead of the Beast Miao King and me. Even White Tiger—a spiritual creature with white fur to boast of—could not catch up.

[P118]
If anything, White Tiger was growing more anxious by the moment.

[P119]
*No wonder. That’s no ordinary tiger.*

[P120]
A *mountain lord* was not just the king of a mountain. The term could also refer to a mountain spirit. But that creature was no spirit of Ailao Mountain.

[P121]
It was its wraith. Perhaps something still more ominous: an evil spirit.

[P122]
What we saw as we pursued the Black Tiger only strengthened that thought.

[P123]
“I’ll tear you apart…!”

[P124]
The Beast Miao King’s voice seemed to boil like lava. His furious gaze had fallen on bodies with their limbs hanging limp.

[P125]
In deep valleys. At the edges of cliffs. Beside streams that must once have run clear but were now black with poison…

[P126]
The corpses of Nanman warriors lay along our route like signposts. The wind carried a sickening mix of blood and foul odors.

[P127]
“How dare you? How dare you do this!”

[P128]
A savage wave of qi poured from the Beast Miao King as the horrific sights flashed past us.

[P129]
He was angrier than ever, and his movements grew rougher with it.

[P130]
“You bastard!”

[P131]
*Tap-tap—shreeeek!*

[P132]
He shot forward at a terrifying speed, straight toward the Black Tiger.

[P133]
But his opponent was a creature called Ailao Mountain’s Wraith. A head-on fight might be another matter; in natural physique and speed, the Beast Miao King could not match it.

[P134]
*Papat!*

[P135]
Just as I expected.

[P136]
The Black Tiger, far beyond an ordinary spiritual creature, pulled farther ahead instead of being caught. Soon it vanished into a deep, dark valley.

[P137]
It gave us a look that seemed to say, *Come and get me if you dare.*

[P138]
*What?*

[P139]
Only then did I slow down and look around.

[P140]
Ancient trees and vines crowded every side. Through the hot, mist-laden air came the unmistakable stench of poison.

[P141]
I did not know exactly where we were, but our headlong chase had clearly brought us to the heart of Ailao Mountain.

[P142]
*This…*

[P143]
I had a bad feeling. A very bad feeling.

[P144]
But while I slowed, the Beast Miao King charged straight into the valley without a hint of hesitation.

[P145]
“Great Hero Yayul, wait—!”

[P146]
*Crack!*

[P147]
There was no time to stop him. Even if there had been, he would not have listened.

[P148]
A little anger could wake a dulled mind. Too much could put it to sleep.

[P149]
“Damn it.”

[P150]
I muttered under my breath and looked at White Tiger, which had gone quiet.

[P151]
It was pacing anxiously at the valley entrance where the Beast Miao King had disappeared, as though it had already sensed the danger. When it met my eyes, it shook its head like a person.

[P152]
“Was that supposed to mean it’s dangerous?”

[P153]
*Grrr.*

[P154]
“Look how smart you are. That’s the first time we’ve agreed. But I can’t turn back this time.”

[P155]
*Grrr…*

[P156]
“You don’t have to come. Go back from here, and if you run into your master or anyone else, tell them we’re here.”

[P157]
White Tiger was clever enough to count as a spiritual creature. I trusted it had understood me.

[P158]
As Yayul Mok had done, I gently stroked it between the eyes, then stepped toward the valley.

[P159]
Without a trace of fear.

[P160]
With my head held high.

[P161]
“…”

[P162]
*I’ll make it back alive, right?*

[P163]
[^1]: *San-gun*, literally “mountain lord,” is a traditional epithet for a tiger and can also refer to a mountain spirit.
```

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

All it had left behind was wreckage that looked as though a bomb had gone off, and a spear lying on the ground with its blade shattered.

[P64]
There were no footprints. No bloodstains.

[P65]
*It got beyond the range of my Qi Sense? That quickly?*

[P66]
As I searched the surroundings, the Beast Miao King arrived with White Tiger. Anger and shame mingled on his face.

[P67]
“Where is it?”

[P68]
“It seems to have run away. I can’t find it.”

[P69]
“…Damn it. You saw me at my worst.”

[P70]
“I understand. I mean that.”

[P71]
Mungyeong and Jeok Cheongang had both been shaken for a moment by the Water God Dragon’s Fear.

[P72]
The Beast Miao King was a formidable master, worthy of his place among the Ten Kings. But comparing him to those two, who had reached a realm beyond humanity, would hardly be fair.

[P73]
If anything, he had shaken off the Fear faster than I expected.

[P74]
Maybe growing up in Nanman, surrounded by strange venomous beasts and ferocious animals, had helped. I could not say.

[P75]
What mattered right now was something else.

[P76]
“It’s still alive. There’s no blood, so it doesn’t seem to be hurt.”

[P77]
The Beast Miao King nodded at my quiet words.

[P78]
“I thought as much. When it knew it couldn’t dodge, it bit down on the spearhead at the last moment. A spearhead wreathed in Force, no less. I’ve lived in Nanman all my life, but I’ve never seen or heard of anything like it.”

[P79]
“I don’t think that’s true.”

[P80]
“What do you mean?”

[P81]
“The last part.”

[P82]
Before he could reply, I went on.

[P83]
“You may never have seen one, but you’ve heard of one. I’m sure of it.”

[P84]
We could not sense the Black Tiger for now, but it might spring out at any moment. The Beast Miao King had put his back to mine as we watched our surroundings. At my words, he stiffened.

[P85]
“Could it be…?”

[P86]
“You’re probably thinking of the right thing. Something similar happened in Hubei Province.”

[P87]
“…You mean that imugi?”

[P88]
The words came out like a groan. He continued, “The Murim Alliance mentioned it in a letter. But I thought the story sounded far-fetched.”

[P89]
“Are you really the Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace? Your only son rides around on a White Tiger, and you couldn’t believe that?”

[P90]
“He rides a White Tiger, not an imugi.”

[P91]
“…Ah.”

[P92]
Fair enough.

[P93]
An imugi belonged in myth. Even coming from the Murim Alliance, the story would have been hard to believe.

[P94]
That short answer left me with nothing to say. Then the Beast Miao King asked, “So was the creature we just saw touched by the Southern Heaven Demon Empress too? That witch?”

[P95]
“I can’t be sure. But it’s likely.”

[P96]
Too much about this felt wrong for me to rule it out.

[P97]
Ailao Mountain had been quiet for more than a hundred years, despite once being the Five Poisons Sect’s headquarters. Now a massacre had happened here, and a Black Tiger of astonishing power had appeared. It all reminded me of the Water God Dragon.

[P98]
*Ailao Mountain’s Wraith.*

[P99]
What was it really?

[P100]
And where were the other two hundred warriors who should still have been here? Where were the beasts they commanded?

[P101]
As I scanned the area, my eyes fell on White Tiger.

[P102]
*Grrr.*

[P103]
Having barely recovered from the Fear, it suddenly crouched low and raised its tail high.

[P104]
The Beast Miao King and I understood what that meant and turned at once.

[P105]
Far away, the darkness was rippling.

[P106]
*That’s…!*

[P107]
We had both overlooked something while we talked.

[P108]
An animal’s sense of smell was dozens, even hundreds of times keener than a human’s. A tiger, which usually hunted at night, had a nose to match.

[P109]
Which meant…

[P110]
*White Tiger can smell farther than my Qi Sense can reach.*

[P111]
The moment it clicked, the Beast Miao King and I kicked off the ground together.

[P112]
* * *

[P113]
As we chased it, I learned exactly why people called tigers mountain lords.[^1]

[P114]
*Ah. Look at that fucking bastard.*

[P115]
I swallowed the curse and glared at the black shape racing far ahead.

[P116]
No matter how far we ran along the winding ridges, no matter how many cloud- and mist-covered peaks we crossed, we could not catch it.

[P117]
Its strength, inexhaustible Stamina, and elusive movements kept it ahead of the Beast Miao King and me. Even White Tiger—a spiritual creature with white fur to boast of—could not catch up.

[P118]
If anything, White Tiger was growing more anxious by the moment.

[P119]
*No wonder. That’s no ordinary tiger.*

[P120]
A *mountain lord* was not just the king of a mountain. The term could also refer to a mountain spirit. But that creature was no spirit of Ailao Mountain.

[P121]
It was its wraith. Perhaps something still more ominous: an evil spirit.

[P122]
What we saw as we pursued the Black Tiger only strengthened that thought.

[P123]
“I’ll tear you apart…!”

[P124]
The Beast Miao King’s voice seemed to boil like lava. His furious gaze had fallen on bodies with their limbs hanging limp.

[P125]
In deep valleys. At the edges of cliffs. Beside streams that must once have run clear but were now black with poison…

[P126]
The corpses of Nanman warriors lay along our route like signposts. The wind carried a sickening mix of blood and foul odors.

[P127]
“How dare you? How dare you do this!”

[P128]
A savage wave of qi poured from the Beast Miao King as the horrific sights flashed past us.

[P129]
He was angrier than ever, and his movements grew rougher with it.

[P130]
“You bastard!”

[P131]
*Tap-tap—shreeeek!*

[P132]
He shot forward at a terrifying speed, straight toward the Black Tiger.

[P133]
But his opponent was a creature called Ailao Mountain’s Wraith. A head-on fight might be another matter; in natural physique and speed, the Beast Miao King could not match it.

[P134]
*Papat!*

[P135]
Just as I expected.

[P136]
The Black Tiger, far beyond an ordinary spiritual creature, pulled farther ahead instead of being caught. Soon it vanished into a deep, dark valley.

[P137]
It gave us a look that seemed to say, *Come and get me if you dare.*

[P138]
*What?*

[P139]
Only then did I slow down and look around.

[P140]
Ancient trees and vines crowded every side. Through the hot, mist-laden air came the unmistakable stench of poison.

[P141]
I did not know exactly where we were, but our headlong chase had clearly brought us to the heart of Ailao Mountain.

[P142]
*This…*

[P143]
I had a bad feeling. A very bad feeling.

[P144]
But while I slowed, the Beast Miao King charged straight into the valley without a hint of hesitation.

[P145]
“Great Hero Yayul, wait—!”

[P146]
*Crack!*

[P147]
There was no time to stop him. Even if there had been, he would not have listened.

[P148]
A little anger could wake a dulled mind. Too much could put it to sleep.

[P149]
“Damn it.”

[P150]
I muttered under my breath and looked at White Tiger, which had gone quiet.

[P151]
It was pacing anxiously at the valley entrance where the Beast Miao King had disappeared, as though it had already sensed the danger. When it met my eyes, it shook its head like a person.

[P152]
“Was that supposed to mean it’s dangerous?”

[P153]
*Grrr.*

[P154]
“Look how smart you are. That’s the first time we’ve agreed. But I can’t turn back this time.”

[P155]
*Grrr…*

[P156]
“You don’t have to come. Go back from here, and if you run into your master or anyone else, tell them we’re here.”

[P157]
White Tiger was clever enough to count as a spiritual creature. I trusted it had understood me.

[P158]
As Yayul Mok had done, I gently stroked it between the eyes, then stepped toward the valley.

[P159]
Without a trace of fear.

[P160]
With my head held high.

[P161]
“…”

[P162]
*I’ll make it back alive, right?*

[P163]
[^1]: *San-gun*, literally “mountain lord,” is a traditional epithet for a tiger and can also refer to a mountain spirit.
```

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
